_readme: Source of truth for the Exeter & Topsham family map. Add or edit a place here, then run: python3 scripts/build_exeter_map.py  (rebuilds the site map page, the interactive map, the static PNG, the vault note, and adds map links to every page named below). 'public': false keeps a place off the public site. 'approx': true draws a hollow marker. Coordinates are street-level only — never put house numbers in public text.

places.name: Tresillian, West Avenue
places.public_text: The Silver family home: Clifford and Gladys brought up their children here. Shot up in the Exeter Blitz, May 1942, and still standing.
places.vault_text: 39 West Avenue. Clifford and Gladys Silver's home, where all six children grew up; damaged in the Blitz, 3–4 May 1942; still standing (2022 photo).

places.name: Higher Barracks
places.public_text: "Part of the barracks, full of the army, about 300 yards away from our house" was destroyed in an air raid David watched as a warden in 1942.
places.vault_text: Barracks about 300 yards from Tresillian, partly destroyed in a 1942 raid (David's 1994 tape). Position approximate.

places.name: Bedford Circus
places.public_text: Clifford's dental surgery stood here "until 1942". The Georgian circus was gutted in the Blitz and later demolished; Princesshay now covers the site.
places.vault_text: 3 Bedford Circus: Clifford's dental surgery until the Blitz of May 1942. Demolished; site now Princesshay.

places.name: Exeter School of Art (Royal Albert Memorial Museum building)
places.public_text: David spent about two terms at the Exeter School of Art before joining the RAF.
places.vault_text: David at Exeter School of Art, c. 1942–43, before the RAF. The school was then in the RAMM building, Queen Street.

places.name: Mona Lodge, Lyndhurst Road
places.public_text: Rupert Philip Acott's house, with lions on the gateposts, and Gladys's childhood home. Muriel Acott was married from here. Still standing.
places.vault_text: Rupert & Charlotte Acott's house; Gladys's childhood home; Muriel's wedding to Basil Scholfield; Clifford photographed Charlotte's room here c. 1905. Still standing (2022 photo).
vault: Old Silver Photos (Acott & Silver family archive)

places.name: Velwell Road, St David's
places.public_text: Clifford and Gladys's home after Tresillian. David saved the family photographs from here "when my mother died".
places.vault_text: 64 Velwell Road: Clifford and Gladys's home by Feb 1951; David's Bristol letters went here; the Old Silver photos were saved from here "before James' bonfire".
vault: Old Silver Photos (Acott & Silver family archive)
Letters from David Silver at Bristol (1947–1953)

places.name: St David's Church
places.public_text: David Silver and Anthea Leigh were married in a side chapel here at the end of December 1952, with James as best man.
places.vault_text: David & Anthea's wedding, side chapel, end of Dec 1952 (probably 31 Dec), James best man.
vault: Letters from David Silver at Bristol (1947–1953)

places.name: The Belmont Nursing Home
places.public_text: Anthea Leigh was born here on 30 April 1928, in "a beautiful Georgian terrace in Exeter, later destroyed in the blitz". Position approximate.
places.vault_text: Anthea born here 30 Apr 1928 (Mary in 1925). Georgian terrace destroyed in the Blitz. Position approximate (Belmont Road).

places.name: Endsleigh School, Grendon Road
places.public_text: "A girls only day school on the corner of Grendon Road", where Anthea and her sister Mary went until the daylight raids on Exeter.
places.vault_text: Anthea's day school from nearly 9 until 11; left when daylight raids began.

places.name: Alexandra Terrace, Blackboy Road
places.vault_text: 18 Alexandra Terrace: Anthea wrote to David from here, 12 July (1960?), with Tamsin, Bridget and Candy.
vault: Old Silver Photos (Acott & Silver family archive)

places.name: Exeter Higher Cemetery
places.vault_text: David's note: his grandmother Charlotte Acott was "buried in Exeter Cemetery". Which cemetery isn't certain.

places.name: Sundew and the garage, Countess Wear
places.public_text: Tom and Edith Leigh's bungalow and garage on the Countess Wear crossroads, where Anthea was brought home as a baby.
places.vault_text: Tom & Edith Leigh's bungalow and filling station at the Countess Wear crossroads; sold c. 1930.

places.name: Denver House and Denver Nurseries, Denver Road
places.public_text: Thomas Bolt Pyne's house and fruit-tree nursery, employing about thirty men: Anthea's grandparents' home, "big, comfortable and secure".
places.vault_text: Thomas Bolt & Angelina Pyne's house and Denver Nurseries.

places.name: Meadow Hayes
places.public_text: Anthea's childhood home, in the meadow opposite Denver Nurseries, until the family left in 1946. "I still dream about Meadow Hayes."
places.vault_text: The Leigh home (one half; Reg Pyne's family the other), built in Thomas Bolt Pyne's meadow opposite Denver Nurseries. Position approximate.

places.name: Park Field, by the Exeter Road
places.public_text: A sewer trench cut through Park Field, opposite the Pyne nurseries, turned up Romano-British pottery, coins and glass.
places.vault_text: Romano-British finds of 1934–35 in Park Field, opposite Denver Nurseries.

places.name: "Doone", Monmouth Hill
places.public_text: The Leighs' semi-detached house with a long front garden, where Anthea's sister Gillian was born.
places.vault_text: "Doone", the Leighs' semi on Monmouth Hill before Meadow Hayes; Gillian born here c. 1935.

places.name: The Strand
places.public_text: Anthea's father worked at Mr Seldon's garage on the Strand, and her godmother Peggy Dolling lived here.
places.vault_text: Mr Seldon's garage (Tom Leigh's job); Peggy Dolling's house, next door to Marion's.

places.name: St Margaret's Church
places.public_text: "The church was the centre of the community": Anthea sang in the choir here for years.
places.vault_text: The Leighs' parish church; Anthea in the choir.

places.name: Rosapenna
places.public_text: Rupert Philip Acott moved to Rosapenna in Topsham after his wife died, and lived there until his death in 1941. Exact location not yet found.
places.vault_text: Rupert Acott's last home, 1921–41 ("still exists", David 1998). Exact location not yet found — marker is a placeholder in Topsham.

places.name: Jenin Cottage
places.vault_text: David and Anthea Silver's home in Topsham, off the High Street, before they moved to Westleigh, Wadebridge, c. 1984. Andy rebuilt the workshop here.

places.name: 43 The Strand (Reka Dom), Flats A and B
places.vault_text: 43 The Strand, EX3 0AY. Andy and Tamsin rented Flat A before Jago was born, then Flat B (43B) from 1979 until the move to Cornwall, Oct 1990. Jago's childhood home.
